title: Should prerequisite knowledge be graded or crisp? Quantifying what thresholding and t-norm path inference cost in log-derived fuzzy knowledge graphs (code, results and run files)
description: Reference implementation, reproduction scripts and result files for the manuscript submitted to Knowledge-Based Systems: fuzzy-graph modularity and the rank-coded cut audit, the calibrated null test (Algorithm 1), generator shortest paths for t-norm path inference, and the pre-deployment audit (Algorithm 2) as a command-line tool, with every analysis in results/ and results/v4/ to results/v14/. Release 4.11.0 answers the ninth review: step 3 of Algorithm 2 takes the Leiden resolution gamma (fuzzykg/audit.py, scripts/fkg_audit.py --gamma) and is re-run on the thirteen real graphs at gamma 0.5, 1 and 2 (results/v14/gamma_step3.json); gamma 1 reproduces all 39 decisions, gamma 0.5 and 2 change 9 and 8 of them, at the median and upper quartile of the dense graphs and at the 2009 and 2015 KC-level transition graphs, while the dense lower-quartile cuts, the Junyi transition cuts and the MOOCCubeX cuts keep their decisions. Release 4.10.0 answers the eighth review: where the no-cut drop of step 3 exceeds 0.05 (only under the cube rescaling) the absolute drops are read as well and a cut is flagged when either reading flags it, which leaves the cube rescaling unrejected by the Junyi topic check and the range of sparse lower-quartile flags at four to seven of seven; step 4 compares the external grouping with a permutation reference, and an undecided cut is resolved by step 4 only when the grouping is matched above that reference (results/v13/absolute_reading.json). Release 4.9.0 answers the seventh review: step 3 of Algorithm 2 now reads a cut by the unit of the memberships (where the unit is arbitrary, a cut is cut only when the Q_F drop and the rank-coded drop both pass, and is undecided when they disagree), fuzzykg/audit.py and scripts/fkg_audit.py take a unit argument and report a decision per cut and a warning for large no-cut drops, the decisions and cells near a threshold are in results/v12/unit_rule.json, the cost of step 3 with 20 seeds is measured, and scripts/INDEX.md lists every script by function. Release 4.8.1 adds the measured cost of the refined tilt grid and the co-practice run of the retrained baselines to release 4.8.0, which adds the analyses that answer the sixth review: the cut audit of Algorithm 2 (step 3) over 20 seeds with both partitions re-drawn per seed, under three increasing rescalings of the memberships and for the rank-coded drop, the sensitivity of the flagging rule to its multiplier and minimum excess, the seed uncertainty of the Junyi topic agreement, and the grade-preserving baselines retrained with every evaluation pair kept out of the sampled non-edges (results/v11); fuzzykg/audit.py now applies the minimum excess of 0.01 of the manuscript and 20 seeds by default. Release 4.7.0 adds the analyses that answer the fifth review: membership-free link-prediction heuristics and a paired comparison with the grade-preserving models on the hidden MOOCCubeX edges, the partition half of the audit on CN15k, and Fig. 4 with the decision guide renumbered (results/v10). Release 4.6.0 added the analyses that answer the fourth review of the Knowledge-Based Systems version: two grade-preserving baselines (a UKGE-style embedding and a GCN encoder with a bilinear decoder, fuzzykg/embeddings.py), the audit on two graded knowledge graphs outside education (PPI5k and CN15k from UKGE), the measured time and memory of the full audit on the largest graph, an analysis of why max-min erases the graded evidence on the dense Junyi graph, and Fig. 4 (results/v9). Release 4.5.0 held the analyses behind the third-revision manuscript: the weighted SBM with 100 refits per null and empirical p-values, the nested SBM with the membership covariate passed to graph-tool through the base state (earlier nested fits had silently ignored it), a clipping check, the decision floor with ten planted graphs for the Junyi co-practice graph and all twelve transition-construction variants, and the seed dispersion of the Q_F drop behind step 3 of Algorithm 2. Datasets are not redistributed; see data/README.md.
